sentences.text:
Suresh Agarwal @ Suresh Kumar Agarwal vs Unknown on 26
June, 2020
Author: Sanjib Banerjee
Bench: Sanjib Banerjee
rc Crm 4454 of 2020 with Cran 2608 of 2020 (Via Video Conference)

In Re: - An application for
anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in connection with Posta
Police Station Case No. 38 of 2020 dated 12.03.2020 under Sections 120/269/273 of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860.
And In the matter of: Suresh Agarwal @ Suresh Kumar Agarwal ....Petitioner.
Mr. Shiladitya Banerjee ...for the Petitioner.
Mr. S.S.Imam Mr. Subrata Roy ...for the State.
The petitioner undertakes to affirm and stamp the petition as per the Rules within 48 hours of resumption of normal functioning of the court.
The petition is taken up through video conference on the basis of such undertaking.
The petitioner claims that certain samples were drawn from the petitioner's shop and the goods were apparently seized but left in the custody of the petitioner.
A subsequent complaint has been lodged on the allegation that some of the samples reveal sub- standard goods.

The petitioner says that sub-standard goods cannot be understood to imply spurious goods as the expressions "sub- standard" and "spurious" have been defined in the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006.
The State says that what was discovered was that harmful substance was being sold and such substance was not fit for human consumption.
The State says that unless the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is permitted, the source of the evil cannot be rooted out.
Since the charge is only of sub-standard goods and not of spurious goods, the custodial interrogation of the petitioner may be unnecessary.

sentences.text:
1 In the event of arrest, the petitioner will be enlarged on bail upon furnishing security of Rs.
50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) together with personal release bond of equivalent value to the satisfaction of the arresting officer.

The petitioner will comply with the conditions laid down in Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and will report to the Investigating Officer as and when called, till the investigation is completed.
In addition, the petitioner will not leave the areas covered by the Commissionerates of Kolkata and Bidhannagar without the previous written permission of the Investigating Officer.
CRM 4454 of 2020 along with CRAN 2608 of 2020 are disposed of.

(Sanjib Banerjee, J.) (Shekhar B. Saraf, J.)
